title: ci-wait-state.mts's wider FAILURE_STATES vocabulary can mis-tie against protocol-helpers.mts's narrower ciStateTieRank
body:
## Background

Surfaced during an E2 critique pass on PR #1502 (issue #1478's fix for
`ci-wait-state.mts`'s multi-instance stale-rollup defect). That fix reuses
`protocol-helpers.mts`'s already-tested `selectLatestCheckInstance` (its
tie-break: still-incomplete wins over completed; else latest `completedAt`
wins; a same-instant tie resolves via `ciStateTieRank`, which special-cases
only two literal strings — `'FAILURE'` (rank 0, always wins) and
`'CANCELLED'` (rank 2, always loses) — with every other state falling into
a generic rank-1 bucket broken by raw lexicographic string comparison).

`ci-wait-state.mts`'s own `FAILURE_STATES` set (around line 178) is wider
than the literal `'FAILURE'` string `ciStateTieRank` special-cases: it also
includes `TIMED_OUT`, `ACTION_REQUIRED`, `STARTUP_FAILURE`, `STALE`, and the
StatusContext-only `ERROR`. When two check-run instances for one required
check name tie on an identical `completedAt` (to-the-second resolution),
and one instance's raw `state` is one of those non-`FAILURE` failure-family
values while the other is a success-family state (`SUCCESS`, `NEUTRAL`,
`SKIPPED`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`), `ciStateTieRank` cannot tell them apart from
an ordinary rank-1 pending/success state, so the tie resolves by raw
lexicographic string comparison instead of "the failure should win."

Independently traced through `ciStateTieRank` + `isNewerCheckInstance`
(`src/scripts/protocol-helpers.mts` lines ~1925-1971) by hand:

- `TIMED_OUT` loses a same-instant tie against **all four** success-family
  states (`'T' > 'S'` and `'T' > 'N'` lexicographically) — silently masked
  as success.
- `STARTUP_FAILURE` and `STALE` each lose against three of the four
  (`NEUTRAL`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `SKIPPED`; each ties `'S...' < 'SUCCESS'` on
  the second character and so happens to still win against `SUCCESS`
  specifically) — masked in the other three cases.
- `ACTION_REQUIRED` and `ERROR` happen to be safe (both start with a letter
  lexicographically before every success-family state's first letter), so
  they always win a same-instant tie already — no defect for those two.

This is the same class of false-green bug #1478/#1471 exist to prevent,
just occurring one layer deeper (inside the shared tie-break's same-instant
fallback) instead of in the raw undeduped list.

## Why this was deferred rather than fixed inline on PR #1502

- **Narrow reachability**: requires two *completed* instances of one
  required check name landing at the exact same recorded second, with
  differing terminal conclusions. `ciStateTieRank`'s own doc comment
  already argues this is "practically never" reached even for the two
  states (`FAILURE`/`CANCELLED`) it does special-case — the same rarity
  class as the already-accepted, cross-referenced `#1483` limitation.
- **Not on the merge-gate path**: `buildCiWaitStateSummary` has no caller
  outside its own CLI entry point and its test file (confirmed via
  `grep -rln "buildCiWaitStateSummary" src/scripts/*.mts`) — in particular,
  `pre-merge-readiness.mts` does not call it. F2's actual merge gate goes
  through the separate `classifyCiChecks` / `summarizeRequiredChecks` path.
  So even in the rare trigger case, the blast radius is confined to the
  D-phase polling/snapshot helper reporting a slightly-early "success" one
  poll cycle sooner than it should — F2 re-evaluates required checks
  independently before merge and is unaffected.
- **The real fix sits in shared, forbidden-to-touch territory for #1478**:
  correcting this properly means teaching `ciStateTieRank` (in
  `protocol-helpers.mts`) about a wider failure-state vocabulary, or
  otherwise changing its rank assignment — but `ciStateTieRank` sits
  directly upstream of `classifyCiChecks` in the call chain, and #1478's
  acceptance criteria hard-required "no change to `classifyCiChecks` /
  `resolvePresentRunConclusion`." Widening the shared tie-break's behavior
  is genuinely separate work with its own blast-radius analysis, not a
  same-PR add-on.

## Proposed change (for whoever picks this up)

One reasonable shape, evaluated during triage but not implemented here —
treat as a starting point, not a spec:

- In `ci-wait-state.mts`, wrap each `CiWaitCheckEntry` passed into the
  dedup reducer with a *tie-break-only* normalized state (leave `CANCELLED`
  as `CANCELLED`; normalize every other entry whose already-computed
  `status === 'failure'` to the literal string `'FAILURE'` before calling
  the shared `selectLatestCheckInstance`), then map the winner back to its
  original entry. This stays entirely local to `ci-wait-state.mts` and
  does not touch `ciStateTieRank` / `classifyCiChecks` /
  `resolvePresentRunConclusion` at all.
- Alternatively (or additionally), consider whether `protocol-helpers.mts`'s
  own failure vocabulary should be widened to match, in a separate,
  carefully-scoped change that explicitly re-verifies `classifyCiChecks`'s
  observable behavior is unchanged for every existing caller.

Either direction needs its own regression tests reproducing a same-instant
tie between a non-`FAILURE`-literal failure state and a success state, and
should re-verify `classifyCiChecks`'s full existing test suite stays green
if the shared tie-break is touched at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A same-instant `completedAt` tie between a `TIMED_OUT` (or
      `STARTUP_FAILURE` / `STALE`) instance and a success-family instance
      for the same required check name no longer resolves to a passing
      status in `buildCiWaitStateSummary`.
- [ ] Regression tests cover at least the `TIMED_OUT`-vs-`SUCCESS` same-
      instant tie (the case with zero incidental protection today).
- [ ] If the fix touches `protocol-helpers.mts`'s shared tie-break
      (`ciStateTieRank` / `isNewerCheckInstance` / `selectLatestCheckPerName`
      / `selectLatestCheckInstance`), `classifyCiChecks`'s full existing
      test suite (`tests/required-checks-summary.test.mts`,
      `tests/advisory-wait.test.mts`) stays green with no behavior change
      for any existing caller/scenario.
- [ ] Existing test suite and `pre-push-validate` pass.

---

_Surfaced during an E2 critique pass on PR #1502 (issue #1478). Flagging
`status:authoring` rather than ready-to-execute: a correct fix may need to
touch shared tie-break code that sits upstream of the merge-gate's own
`classifyCiChecks` path, which needs its own careful blast-radius review
before an autonomous session executes it — not a same-shape drop-in like
#1478 itself was._

Refs #1478
